drifted.spec_text: The actor service thread MUST be pinned to a core in the same NUMA zone as the NVMe controller device. ... SC-007: The actor thread runs on a core in the same NUMA zone as the controller, verified at instantiation.
drifted.actual: probe_controller() hardcodes the discovered NUMA node to 0 for every controller (comment: "NUMA node is not available from minimal bindings; default to 0"). set_actor_cpu()/initialize() then pick target_cpu from this always-0 snapshot.numa_node, so the actor is only correctly NUMA-pinned when the real controller happens to be on node 0; on any device attached to a non-zero NUMA node the thread is pinned to the wrong zone with no error or warning.

drifted.spec_text: System MUST expose device information (capacity, max queue depth, IO queue count, max transfer size, block/sector size, NUMA id, NVMe version) via the IBlockDevice interface. ... SC-005: Device information queries return values consistent with the physical hardware properties of the bound NVMe controller.
drifted.actual: NvmeController::attach() hardcodes nvme_version to NvmeVersion{major:1,minor:0,tertiary:0} and max_transfer_size to a fixed 131072 (128KB) for every controller, with the comment "Default version and transfer size (not available from minimal bindings)". These two fields are never read from real Identify Controller data, unlike num_io_queues/max_queue_depth which are read from real SPDK opts a few lines above. Any controller with a different NVMe spec version or MDTS-derived max transfer size will report incorrect values.

drifted.spec_text: When compiled with the telemetry feature, system MUST collect and expose min/max/mean IO latencies... SC-008: All public interface methods have unit tests and documentation tests.
drifted.actual: telemetry.rs::TelemetryStats::record() takes 3 parameters (latency_ns, bytes, is_read), but the #[cfg(feature="telemetry")] tests stats_record_single_op and stats_record_multiple_ops call stats.record(1000, 4096) with only 2 arguments. This fails to compile with --features telemetry (confirmed: cargo test -p block-device-spdk-nvme --features telemetry --no-run -> 4x error[E0061] this method takes 3 arguments but 2 arguments were supplied). The telemetry feature's own test suite is broken, violating the SC-008 test-coverage requirement for this feature-gated code path. Default (non-telemetry) build/tests compile cleanly, confirming this is isolated to the telemetry feature.

unspecced.suggested_spec: Add to FR-021: signal_stop() closes the actor's command channel without joining, allowing all actors on a controller to be signalled before any is joined/detached.
Add to FR-021: detach_controller() drops the parked controller (spdk_nvme_detach) and must be called after shutdown() due to the component's intentional Arc-cycle leak.
New FR: the actor MUST rotate its starting client index each poll cycle so no single client is perpetually serviced first, preventing head-of-line starvation of later clients.
New FR: bound the number of commands drained from a single client's ingress channel per poll cycle to preserve fairness across clients sharing one actor thread.

unspecced.feature: Graceful drain on actor stop (5s deadline, Aborted completions for pending ops)
unspecced.suggested_spec: New FR: on shutdown, the actor MUST attempt to drain in-flight operations for up to 5 seconds, delivering Completion::Error{Aborted} for any operations still pending when the deadline expires.

unspecced.feature: Controller parking for safe detach ordering
unspecced.suggested_spec: Document as part of the signal_stop/shutdown/detach_controller lifecycle FR: the controller handle is parked (not dropped) at actor stop so detach_controller() can safely perform spdk_nvme_detach after the thread has joined.

New FR in spec 002: --device-count N attaches to and benchmarks N devices concurrently, scaling worker threads across devices, with results aggregated across all devices.
